items.label: f01-pipeline
items.front: What are the stages of the OpsForge operations pipeline, and which is real today?
items.back: Validate, rate-limit (per operator and command), approve if needed, simulate (dry run), queue (BullMQ), execute in the worker, audit, roll back. Most stages are stubs; requiresApproval is the one real policy line, and executeOperation just returns status queued.

items.label: f03-separation-of-duties
items.front: How do rbac.ts and the approval policy implement separation of duties?
items.back: ops_engineer has operations.execute but not operations.approve, while ops_lead has both. requiresApproval routes deletions and bulk operations (> 100 targets) to a second person, so the one who fires a dangerous operation is not the only one who can bless it.

items.label: f02-flag-rules
items.front: How does evaluateFlag combine targeting rules and their conditions?
items.back: Rules are ORed with .some(): any matching rule turns the flag on. Inside a rule, each specified condition (plan, region, customerIds) is ANDed through early return false; conditions a rule does not specify are skipped. An empty rule list is false.

items.prompt: A percentage flag is enabled with rolloutPercentage 0. Which customers get it?

choices.text: About 1%, since bucket 0 still counts as in
All of them, as 0 is read as no limit set
Only customers whose id hashes exactly to 0
None of them, since a bucket is never below 0

choices: About 1%, since bucket 0 still counts as in
All of them, as 0 is read as no limit set
Only customers whose id hashes exactly to 0
None of them, since a bucket is never below 0

items.explanation: hashToBucket returns Math.abs(hash % 100), a value from 0 to 99, and the check is bucket < rolloutPercentage. No bucket is less than 0, so nobody gets the flag; with 100, everybody does.

items.prompt: classifySeverity(0.5) is called for an error rate of exactly 50%. Which severity comes back?

choices.text: sev1, since 0.5 reaches the sev1 cut-off
sev2, since 0.5 is not greater than 0.5
sev4, as exact values fall through to it
sev3, as only rates over 0.5 count as high

choices: sev1, since 0.5 reaches the sev1 cut-off
sev2, since 0.5 is not greater than 0.5
sev4, as exact values fall through to it
sev3, as only rates over 0.5 count as high

items.explanation: Every threshold uses a strict >. 0.5 > 0.5 is false, then 0.5 > 0.2 is true, so the result is sev2. Only a rate above 0.5 is sev1.

items.prompt: Session data says the role is "auditor", which is not in rolePermissions. What does hasPermission(role, "audit.read") return?

choices.text: false, from the ?? false deny-by-default
true, as unknown roles inherit viewer rights
true, since every role may read audit logs
It throws, as rolePermissions[role] is undefined

choices: false, from the ?? false deny-by-default
true, as unknown roles inherit viewer rights
true, since every role may read audit logs
It throws, as rolePermissions[role] is undefined

items.explanation: rolePermissions["auditor"] is undefined, so the optional chain ?.includes yields undefined and ?? false turns that into false. Nothing throws, and there is no fallback role.

items.prompt: A targeted flag has rules [{ plan: "enterprise" }, { region: "eu-west" }]. A customer is on plan "pro" in region "eu-west". What does evaluateFlag return?

choices.text: true, but only after a percentage bucket check
false, because both rules have to match together
true, because the second rule matches on its own
false, because the customer is not on enterprise

choices: true, but only after a percentage bucket check
false, because both rules have to match together
true, because the second rule matches on its own
false, because the customer is not on enterprise

items.explanation: Rules are combined with .some(), an OR: the first rule fails on plan, the second has only a region condition, which matches, so the result is true. Conditions inside one rule are ANDed; separate rules are not.

items.prompt: A flag has isEnabled true, flagType "targeted" and targetingRules []. Who gets the feature?

choices.text: Everybody, as no rules means no restrictions
Nobody, as .some() on an empty array is false
Only customers on the default plan and region
Whoever falls under its rolloutPercentage value

choices: Everybody, as no rules means no restrictions
Nobody, as .some() on an empty array is false
Only customers on the default plan and region
Whoever falls under its rolloutPercentage value

items.explanation: The targeted branch returns flag.targetingRules.some(...). Array.prototype.some on an empty array returns false, so the flag is off for every customer. rolloutPercentage is used only by the percentage type.

items.prompt: A signed-out visitor requests /login-history. What does the root middleware do?

choices.text: Redirects to /login?next=%2Flogin-history
Lets it through, as it starts with "/login"
Answers 401 with an UNAUTHORIZED envelope
Lets it through only for GET requests here

choices: Redirects to /login?next=%2Flogin-history
Lets it through, as it starts with "/login"
Answers 401 with an UNAUTHORIZED envelope
Lets it through only for GET requests here

items.explanation: isPublic is publicRoutes.some(route => pathname.startsWith(route)). "/login-history" starts with "/login", so it counts as public and NextResponse.next() runs. The guide explains the prefix match for /api/auth sub-paths; it also makes any path beginning with /login public.

items.prompt: requiresApproval("billing.refund", 100) is called for a refund to exactly 100 customers. What is the result?

choices.text: false, since the check is targetCount > 100
true, because every refund needs approval
true, since the check is targetCount >= 100
false, because refunds are never approved

choices: false, since the check is targetCount > 100
true, because every refund needs approval
true, since the check is targetCount >= 100
false, because refunds are never approved

items.explanation: The bulk rule is a strict greater-than, so exactly 100 targets do not trigger it, and "billing.refund" does not contain "delete". 101 targets would require approval.

items.prompt: At runtime in this repo, what does getCommand("customer.suspend") return?

choices.text: A default no-op command that just logs the payload
undefined, as registerCommand is never called anywhere
It throws Unknown command with the key in the text
The customer_suspend command, registered on import

choices: A default no-op command that just logs the payload
undefined, as registerCommand is never called anywhere
It throws Unknown command with the key in the text
The customer_suspend command, registered on import

items.explanation: registry is an empty Map until registerCommand runs, and no file in src or worker calls registerCommand. getCommand is a plain Map lookup, so it returns undefined instead of throwing; callers must handle that.

items.prompt: A flag has flagType "boolean" and isEnabled false. What does evaluateFlag return for any customer?

choices.text: true, as boolean flags are always on
It depends on the targeting rules
false, from the first guard clause
It depends on the customer bucket

choices: true, as boolean flags are always on
It depends on the targeting rules
false, from the first guard clause
It depends on the customer bucket

items.explanation: The first line is if (!flag.isEnabled) return false, so a disabled flag is off whatever its type. A boolean flag returns true only when it is enabled.

items.prompt: Which role in rbac.ts holds customers.write but not operations.execute?

choices.text: finance
viewer
support
ops_engineer

choices: finance
viewer
support
ops_engineer

items.explanation: support has dashboard.read, customers.read, customers.write, incidents.manage and audit.read. viewer and finance cannot write customers, and ops_engineer can both write customers and execute operations.

items.prompt: A signed-out visitor requests /customers/cus_001. Where does the middleware send them?

choices.text: To / first, which then forwards on to the /login page
To /login with next set to /customers/cus_001
To /login, with no record of the page they wanted
Nowhere: the page itself renders its own login form

choices: To / first, which then forwards on to the /login page
To /login with next set to /customers/cus_001
To /login, with no record of the page they wanted
Nowhere: the page itself renders its own login form

items.explanation: The middleware builds new URL("/login", req.url), sets the next search param to the original pathname and redirects; the response also carries the x-request-id header. The login page can then return the user to where they were going.

items.prompt: An operator runs a new command keyed "customer.purge" against 50 customers. What does requiresApproval("customer.purge", 50) return?

choices.text: false, as the key has no "delete" and 50 is not > 100
true, since purge is listed as a dangerous verb in policy
true, as every customer.* command needs a second human
false, but only because the dangerLevel column is low

choices: false, as the key has no "delete" and 50 is not > 100
true, since purge is listed as a dangerous verb in policy
true, as every customer.* command needs a second human
false, but only because the dangerLevel column is low

items.explanation: The policy is command.includes("delete") || targetCount > 100. "customer.purge" does not contain "delete" and 50 is not above 100, so no approval is required: the substring loophole the chapter asks you to find. dangerLevel is not consulted at all.

items.prompt: A targeted flag has a single rule { plan: "pro", region: "us-east" }. A customer is on plan "pro" in region "eu-west". What does evaluateFlag return?

choices.text: true: plan matches, which is enough for a single rule
false: plan rules only apply to the enterprise plan
true: region is ignored whenever plan is also present
false: the region check returns false inside the rule

choices: true: plan matches, which is enough for a single rule
false: plan rules only apply to the enterprise plan
true: region is ignored whenever plan is also present
false: the region check returns false inside the rule

items.explanation: Inside a rule every specified condition must hold, because each mismatch returns false early. plan matches but region differs, so the only rule fails and .some() returns false.
